lines.en: Good morning, Max. Come in. **What’s the matter?**

Meu estômago dói e eu me sinto cansado.

lines.en: **How long have you had** this pain?
lines.pt: Há quanto tempo você está com essa dor?

lines.en: Since last night. It’s about a five.
lines.pt: Desde ontem à noite. É uns cinco.

lines.en: I’ll give you a prescription. Take it to the pharmacy.
lines.pt: Vou dar a você uma receita. Leve à farmácia.

lines.en: Thanks. **How often should I take** it?

lines.en: Yes, ten o’clock. If it’s an emergency, **call 911.**
lines.pt: Sim, às dez. Se for uma emergência, ligue para o 911.

pages.title: Real-Life Mission Day 5

unit.name: Health & body
map: Asking for help in an emergency

situation.text: A sick day in the United States: you describe your symptoms, see a doctor, ask the pharmacist about your medicine and book a follow-up appointment. One day, many real situations.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can move through a whole sick day in English: describe it, ask the right questions, get your medicine and book what comes next — and ask for help if it is an emergency.
canDo: Describe symptoms: My… hurts / I feel…
Ask the doctor and the pharmacist: How long…? How often should I take…?
Book a follow-up: I’d like to make an appointment
Ask for help: Call 911! / It’s an emergency
success: I ask how often to take it.
I know what to say in an emergency.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — A sick day, step by step
pages.intro: A sick day in the USA has steps: tell someone what hurts, see a doctor, get medicine at the pharmacy and book a follow-up. Look and guess before you read.

cards.pt: Farmácia: sem receita ou com receita
cards.note: Some medicine is on the shelf; other medicine needs a prescription. Ask the pharmacist.
You check in, show your card and say what is the matter.
You can book by phone or app. In an emergency, you call 911.

qs.q: What do you do first on a sick day?
qs.pt: O que você faz primeiro num dia de doença?

levels.B1: I describe my symptoms and book an appointment.
levels.B2: You describe what is wrong and choose between a pharmacy, an appointment or, if needed, an emergency call.

levels.A2: At the pharmacy, with or without a prescription.
levels.B1: At the pharmacy: some medicine is OTC, some needs a prescription.
levels.B2: The pharmacist can answer questions about how to use a medicine and what the label says.

levels.A2: In an emergency, for an ambulance.
levels.B1: When someone is in danger, hurt or very sick.
levels.B2: You call 911 for an emergency, say what happened and where you are, and stay on the line.

pages.compare: In Brazil you can also go to a pharmacy, a clinic or call 192 in an emergency. What is the first step on a sick day where you live?

pages.title: Group mission — a sick day
pages.goal: Each group chains several situations of the unit into one sick day, in English, and solves the small problems along the way.

missions.mission: Describe a stomach ache to the doctor. Then go to the pharmacy with a prescription and ask how often to take it. Finally, book a follow-up.
missions.constraint: Use “How long…?” and “How often should I…?”

missions.mission: Call a clinic and make an appointment. The day is full: choose another. Then ask the pharmacist something for a headache and if it is safe.
missions.constraint: Use “Are you free on…?” and “Is it safe…?”

missions.mission: At the park you see someone hurt. Call 911, say where you are, then later tell a friend about it and book your own check-up.
missions.constraint: Use “It’s an emergency!” and “I’d like to make an appointment.”

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Use short phrases for the whole situation.

ladder.say: My stomach hurts and I feel tired. I’d like to make an appointment.
I’ve had a stomach ache since last night, so I’d like to see a doctor as soon as possible.
ladder.goal: Explain a situation and a request.

ladder.say: I wasn’t sure whether to go to the pharmacy first or book a visit, so I called to ask what you’d recommend.
ladder.goal: Describe decisions and ask for guidance.

ladder.say: Given how long it has lasted, I’d rather have it looked at properly than keep waiting it out.
I’d hate to make a fuss over nothing, but I’d feel better knowing it’s been looked at.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
